title: Coverage Summary
intro: 228 names under coverage, classified on two axes. Axis 1 is business durability — how likely the business is to become useless (reviewed per ticker by the daily classification routine: durable franchise, cyclical, AI-exposed, structurally challenged, turnaround, special situation). Axis 2 is price — downside room and asymmetry from the model's own numbers (Ratio B, distance to the EPP panic floor, adjusted-vs-market composite, conservative 2-yr case). Today: 35 compounders at a low price, 7 in the AI-fear basket, 40 quality names neutrally valued, 50 priced for perfection, 46 with too much cycle risk, 26 cyclicals at a fair or discounted price, and 24 structural, turnaround or special situations. Everything below is a model output, not a price target. Six durability calls changed today. Booking leaves the compounder list for the AI-fear basket: travel demand is unchanged, yet the stock sits in the bottom quartile of its range at Ratio B 0.41x and a +0.60 model-vs-market gap, and that discount is the agentic-travel-assistant debate, not the cycle. Starbucks goes the other way, from turnaround to durable franchise on two straight quarters of US traffic growth (+7.1% US, +7.9% global comps) - but at Ratio B 2.63x and 104% above its floor it is now a durable business at a bad price, so it moves from the turnaround list to the sell list. Pfizer stops being filed as structurally challenged: alone among that group it carries a 3.05 proxy composite and a +0.62 gap, and the model names the Seagen ADC platform in the 53% bull case - a patent cycle to underwrite, not secular decline, which is exactly what separates it from Bristol, whose own base case is simply pre-cliff earnings. Estee Lauder was carrying a profile describing a different company; it is now classified as what it is, a prestige-beauty franchise with intact brands and broken GAAP earnings. Volkswagen stops being called a turnaround - simultaneous China share loss across VW, Audi and Porsche plus a EUR4-5bn tariff burden is a permanently lower earnings base - and Warner Bros Discovery's obsolescence risk drops to 2 after Paramount settled with 12 state AGs on Sept 21.

sections.heading: Best buys — durable businesses with limited downside
body: Downside limited by the model's own floor and asymmetry, AND low-to-neutral risk of the business becoming useless. Ranked by a blend of model-vs-market gap, Ratio B, conservative 2-yr return, distance to floor and obsolescence risk. Buys at today's prices, not on a further pullback.

items.x: The single widest mispricing in coverage: adjusted composite sits +1.94 above the market-implied composite with Ratio B at 0.02x, because the price ($147.61) is still pinned to the $144 bear case after the Sept 17 low of $139. The $664B RPO and $30B+ of newly signed AI cloud contracts are real; so is BBB- credit, $125B+ debt and negative FCF funding the buildout. Buy the gap, size for the balance sheet.

Priced 1.5% above its $271 earnings-power floor with 24% downside against 111% upside (Ratio B 0.22x) and a +1.11 gap. The Sept 8 supply-chain disclosure did the de-rating; FY2026 organic growth guidance of 8.3-9.3% and the MAKO installed base did not change. Best risk/reward in medtech.

Gap of +1.49 - adjusted composite 3.22 against a market-implied 1.73 - with 28.6% downside and 96.4% upside. The stock is consolidating at its 52-week low on competitive-intensity worries while guidance and the FWA share-gain thesis are untouched. Buy.

8.8% downside to bear against 59.2% upside, 7.2% above the $277.20 floor, conservative 2-yr +34%. You are being paid to wait out a frozen housing market at a price that already assumes it stays frozen. Buy.

7.1% above its floor with Ratio B 0.22x and a +0.73 gap. Fee-based broking and consulting with a 19-year margin-expansion streak; the Sept 16 CEO appointment of Matt Stadler is the only thing to watch. Buy.

Trading 0.5% above its earnings-power floor after a -4.8% week to $69.80, with a +0.81 gap and Ratio B 0.33x. FY2026 operating EPS guidance of $4.28-$4.40 is reaffirmed and the 6-8% growth guide is intact - this is a regulated utility plus nuclear at its floor. Buy.

The only compounder in coverage trading *below* its earnings-power floor (-11.5%), with Ratio B 0.20x and a +0.67 gap. A ratings duopoly plus the index flywheel, now extending into on-chain risk assessment via OpenZeppelin. Buy.

Gap +1.01, Ratio B 0.43x (39.4% downside against 91.0% upside), conservative 2-yr +17%. Fee-related earnings from the insurance balance sheet are the durable half; realizations are the cyclical half, and the price is paying for neither. Buy.
12.9% above floor, Ratio B 0.20x, gap +0.84. Counter-cyclical auto-parts retail into a Q4 print due Sept 22 (~$54.97 consensus EPS, +12.9% YoY). EV mix is a decade-long headwind, not a 2027 one. Buy.
19.5% downside against 49.2% upside with a +0.93 gap. Landfill scarcity plus pricing power; the only caveat is that at 74.5% above its $121 floor the cushion is the moat, not the price. Buy.

sections.heading: Second line — same quality, slightly less asymmetry
body: Also compounders at a low price; buy after the first group.

items.x: Cheapest large pharma in coverage: 15.0% downside against 39.2% upside, 16% above floor, gap +0.64, conservative 2-yr +34%. The Barclays-upgrade bounce has been given back and the ~+10% CER FY2026 EPS guidance raise stands. Buy into the Oct 30 print.

30.4% downside against 79.9% upside (Ratio B 0.38x), gap +0.78, conservative 2-yr +17%. A closed-loop fee flywheel where the only real variable is the credit cycle, and the price is not charging for the flywheel. Buy ahead of Oct 23.

Gap +0.98 with 20.9% downside against 46.5% upside. The pullback is sector rotation out of industrials, not the data-center cooling backlog. The one reservation: 92.4% above the $220 floor, so the margin of safety is the order book rather than the price.

Gap +0.69, Ratio B 0.65x, conservative 2-yr +37%, after the Sept 16-18 slide from EUR951 to EUR879 on India/APAC build-out scrutiny. Single-platform payments growing 20%+ with net cash. Buy the selloff.

The most durable luxury brand in coverage at 25% downside-to-upside (Ratio B 0.25x), 29% above floor, gap +0.26. Middle East slowdown is the reason it is cheap; scarcity is the reason it does not matter.
Ratio B 0.16x with a +0.27 gap at a 52-week low. A franchised royalty stream on 40,000 restaurants priced as though traffic never recovers. Buy.
Gap +0.83 with 57.9% downside against 98.8% upside at record $1.35T AUM. The fee-related half of earnings is an annuity; the realization half is the cycle you are being paid to underwrite. Buy.
Gap +0.90, Ratio B 0.72x, 23.4% above floor. August core net new assets up 46% YoY, and the Fed's Sept 16 hike cuts the bear-case NIM-compression trigger rather than feeding it. Buy.
Gap +0.81 at 20.6% above floor with Ratio B 0.91x. Network duopoly economics; the interchange/regulatory file is the only live risk and it has been live for a decade. Buy.

Ratio B 0.27x and a +0.41 gap after a -2.8% week to $129.87 and a ~9% YTD decline. Elliott is in, Joaquin Duato joined the board Sept 17, and the cost program has not yet shown up in numbers. Buy the activist setup, not the GLP-1 headline.

sections.heading: The AI-fear basket — cheap because the market is pricing disruption
body: Franchises with a live generative-AI substitution debate (software, IT services, information, search, mobility). Kept OUT of the compounder list on purpose: the discount is real and the reported numbers keep refusing the bear case, but this is the one group where 'becoming useless' is a non-zero scenario. Own as a basket, sized as one position, not as single convictions.

items.x: The cleanest name in the AI-fear basket: trading 7.5% *below* its $269.23 earnings-power floor with Ratio B 0.23x and a +1.01 gap, after a Q3 beat-and-raise where AI-first ARR crossed $650M. The market is pricing Sora and Canva taking the creative suite; the reported numbers keep refusing it. The CEO seat fills Dec 1.

Gap +0.94 with Ratio B 0.68x, 29.6% above floor. The bear case is concrete - only ~17 of ~200 planned Joule agents delivered, which drove the Santander/UBS downgrades - but the ERP system of record is the stickiest asset in enterprise software. Own it in the basket.

Moved out of the compounder list today. Ratio B 0.41x, 12.3% above floor, gap +0.60, and sell-side targets 45-60% above spot ($247 Wedbush, $270 Evercore) - yet the stock sits in the 25th percentile of its post-split range with travel demand unchanged. That spread is the agentic-booking debate. Real discount, real risk: own it as part of the basket, not as a standalone conviction.

Gap widened to +0.59 as the software selloff took the stock to $136.04; 44% downside against 103% upside. The de-rating is sector-wide AI-multiple compression, not company news - subscription growth and AI ACV are intact. Basket position.

Gap +0.68, Ratio B 0.68x, 15.9% above floor. TD Cowen initiated Buy on Sept 10-11 arguing the AI-disruption fear is simply not visible in renewals. Professional information with proven pricing - the best fundamentals-to-fear ratio in the basket.

The hardest one to own: gap is -0.20 (fairly valued, not cheap on the composite) even though Ratio B is 0.48x and the conservative 2-yr case is +37%. JPMorgan cut to Neutral and took its target from $605 to $331 because AI substitution has spread past TurboTax into the QuickBooks/GBS core. Smallest position in the basket.

Gap -0.10 and 23.3% above floor with Ratio B 0.45x and conservative 2-yr +11%. Guggenheim's Sept 18 downgrade cited falling job listings and Accenture Edge as evidence of softening large-enterprise demand - the AI-deflation thesis in its most concrete form so far. The $1B/5yr Anthropic partnership is the hedge. Oct 1 print is the test.

sections.heading: Almost there — quality at a neutral price worth adding on weakness

items.x: Widest gap outside Oracle at +1.49 (adjusted composite 3.48 against market-implied 1.99) with 19.4% downside against 80.6% upside, pinned near its 52-week low by refinancing-driven share supply after a Q3 print showing 22.5% revenue growth and raised FY2026 EPS guidance. It stays out of the buy list only because it sits 147% above its $440 floor - proprietary aerospace parts leave nothing underneath.

Gap +1.79 with Ratio B 0.44x, but conservative 2-yr is -17% and the stock is 94.9% above floor. AI semiconductor revenue of $16.7B in the quarter (+221% YoY) against $115B FY2027 / $230B FY2028 targets - the gap is real, the floor is not. Add on weakness, do not chase.
Gap +0.51 and Ratio B 0.48x, but 112.9% above the floor - the best retail franchise in the world with no price support underneath it. FQ4 lands Sept 24. Add on a real drawdown, nothing more.

Gap +0.21, Ratio B 0.76x (40.4% downside against 53.0% upside). Buffett became Chairman Emeritus on Sept 18 with Abel now CEO; the PacifiCorp wildfire appeal is set for Nov 3. Fair price, fortress balance sheet.

Gap +0.46, conservative 2-yr +18%, 26.2% above floor. IBIT inflows and the LifePath launch are working; the DOJ possibly joining the antitrust suit against BlackRock/State Street (Sept 18) is the new overhang. Add on weakness.

sections.heading: Cyclicals where the cycle risk is already in the price
body: Good businesses whose earnings are the cycle, at prices that already discount it. Fine to own, sized as cyclicals.

items.x: Gap +0.76 and conservative 2-yr +24% with Ratio B 0.88x. BofA's own economists pushed the first cut out to July 2027, which is the bull case for NII and the reason to own the cycle here. Size it as a bank, not a compounder.

Now trading 0.8% *below* its $214.50 floor for the first time this cycle after the August combined ratio came in at 89.3% (from 83.1%) and net income fell 22% YoY. The deterioration is non-cat frequency and severity, not a storm - so it is an underwriting-cycle problem, not an event. Gap widened to +0.70 because the market discounted the miss harder than the model did. Accumulate.

Gap +0.30, Ratio B 0.60x, 18.6% above floor. The Crane (TMI Unit 1) restart environmental assessment is the near-term catalyst, with Microsoft, Meta and Walmart PPAs underneath. Earnings still ride power prices - own it sized as a cyclical.

Gap +0.54 with Ratio B 0.62x at the 10th percentile of its 52-week range. Merchant power plus nuclear into AI load growth; the September shelf registration is a mild dilution overhang. Cheapest way in coverage to own the power trade.

Gap +0.52, Ratio B 0.97x, but the conservative 2-yr case is flat (-0%). Record profitability and LatAm growth are in the price near the top of the range; the EUR1.825bn buyback is ~31% done. Own small, do not add.

Gap has narrowed to +0.18 - fairly valued now, not undervalued - at 8.2% above a $205.48 floor, with 55% downside against 73% upside. Data-center revenue growth above 90% YoY and 75% gross margin are unchanged; the price has simply caught up. Hold what you own; Xi's Sept 24 visit is the China-access catalyst.

Gap +0.60 with ROTCE now guided above the 11% target and a $30B buyback authorized. 55% downside against 46% upside keeps it a cyclical, but the restructuring is finally showing in returns. Accumulate.

Gap +0.05 - fairly valued - but only 8.9% above its $96 floor with Ratio B 0.81x, the best downside protection in Materials. Six straight quarters of +4% organic sales and FY26 guidance of $7.70-$8.10 reaffirmed. The cheap option on an industrial/auto recovery.

sections.heading: The model's own BUYs we keep out of the buy list
body: Rated BUY by the valuation model; cheap by the numbers but not downside-limited compounders.

items.x: Gap +1.79 with Ratio B 0.44x, but conservative 2-yr is -17% and the stock is 94.9% above floor. AI semiconductor revenue of $16.7B in the quarter (+221% YoY) against $115B FY2027 / $230B FY2028 targets - the gap is real, the floor is not. Add on weakness, do not chase.

Rated BUY by the valuation model (gap +0.90, Ratio B 0.16x) and deliberately kept out of the buy list. Q2 broadband losses widened to -172K, Wolfe downgraded to Underperform on worsening industry dynamics, and leverage is high. Statistically cheap because the subscriber base is shrinking - that is not a discount, it is a countdown.

Gap +0.94 at trough earnings with Ratio B 0.50x and the 114-year dividend streak intact, but 102.5% above the $14 panic floor and a conservative 2-yr case of just +3%. The ethane advantage is normalising. Cyclical, not a compounder.

Trades 24.3% below its earnings-power floor with a +1.03 gap and 14.9% downside against 104.7% upside - the most asymmetric setup in coverage, and a binary one. SB 492 died on Sept 1 without a liability cap, so California wildfire exposure is uncapped and decided by the legislature. Position size is the whole decision here.

Gap +0.62, 40.7% above floor. The Fengari/Metra acquisition (~2.8bn PLN, debt-funded) buys Western European brands and US entry; FY2026 EBITDA guidance of ~1,112m PLN is reiterated. Note the price ambiguity flagged at refresh (1152 / 1225 / 1265 PLN). Cyclical.

Reclassified today from structurally challenged to a durable franchise at risk 3. It carries a 3.05 proxy composite and a +0.62 gap at 13.1% above its $24.36 floor - the strongest fundamentals reading of any name previously in the structural bucket - and the model's 53.1% bull weight is explicitly the Seagen ADC platform outpacing the Eliquis/Ibrance cliff. It still stays out of the buy list: Ratio B 1.34x gives 58.3% downside against 43.4% upside, and the 2028 cliff is the reason risk stays at 3 rather than 2. Own the yield and the pipeline, not the floor.

Gap +0.75 with Ratio B 0.81x, but 117.6% above floor and 45% realised volatility. FY2026 guidance holds at EUR13.7-14.2bn revenue and ~19% margin; JPMorgan keeps it on Negative Catalyst Watch and the F126 naval program is cancelled. A ceasefire de-rates this 40% overnight - own it as a cyclical, not as a franchise.

Widest gap outside Oracle at +1.49 (adjusted composite 3.48 against market-implied 1.99) with 19.4% downside against 80.6% upside, pinned near its 52-week low by refinancing-driven share supply after a Q3 print showing 22.5% revenue growth and raised FY2026 EPS guidance. It stays out of the buy list only because it sits 147% above its $440 floor - proprietary aerospace parts leave nothing underneath.

sections.heading: Turnarounds and structural risk — cheap is not enough

items.x: Trading 33.5% below its earnings-power floor with a +1.29 gap and Ratio B 0.10x - statistically the cheapest name in coverage. It stays out of the buy list because the CFO said on Sept 9 that fiber-broadband pricing has turned 'irrational' and Q3 subscriber losses will not improve. Parks and NBCU buy time; they do not fix the connectivity core.

33.8% below its $69.35 floor at a fresh 52-week low, Ratio B 0.02x (1.9% downside against 109.2% upside), conservative 2-yr +74%. Every bit of that is price, not proof: the Clover/merchant deceleration is unresolved and Oct 27 is the next evidence. A turnaround bet, sized as one.

Conservative 2-yr +81% with Ratio B 0.25x and a +0.11 gap - fairly valued on the composite, cheap on asymmetry. Lores is cutting 20% of the workforce over 2-3 years and has said PayPal is 'totally open' to external offers. Branded-checkout share loss to Apple Pay and Shop Pay is the unfixed problem.

Rated BUY by the valuation model (gap +0.90, Ratio B 0.16x) and deliberately kept out of the buy list. Q2 broadband losses widened to -172K, Wolfe downgraded to Underperform on worsening industry dynamics, and leverage is high. Statistically cheap because the subscriber base is shrinking - that is not a discount, it is a countdown.

11.2% below its earnings-power floor at a 12-year low of $35.51, gap +0.29, Ratio B 0.36x. The brand is intact; the earnings are not, and removal from the S&P 100 on Sept 21 added flow pressure on top. Buy the floor breach only if you can hold through China.

Gap -0.04 (fairly valued), Ratio B 0.48x, conservative 2-yr -5%. The SPEEA vote on Sept 24-Oct 1 ahead of the Oct 6 contract expiry is the near-term binary; the $36.2bn Korean Air order and the MQ-25A award are the backlog. Not cheap enough yet to pay for the recovery.

14.5% above floor with Ratio B 0.60x and a flat -0.02 gap - and unlike Pfizer it stays structurally challenged, because the model's own base case is just Eliquis growing until the 2027-28 cliff arrives while Cobenfy 'stays sub-scale' in the bear case. Market EV $83.51 sits above proxy EV $80.69: the model is less optimistic than the market. Camzyos has a Sept 30 PDUFA date. Cheap, with the E contested.

Gap +0.26 at 80.6% above floor, conservative 2-yr -6%. The AdX structural-breakup risk is gone (behavioral remedies only), which is why this is no longer a discounted name - it is an AI-exposed franchise at a fair price. Wait for the discount rather than paying up for Gemini.

Reclassified today. The prestige portfolio - La Mer, MAC, Jo Malone, Le Labo - is intact and the FY2027 guide of $3.10-$3.35 EPS is +24-34% YoY off four straight beats, but TTM GAAP EPS is still negative on PRGP restructuring, so the $50 earnings-power floor is not a floor you can lean on. Gap +0.05, Ratio B 1.09x: a turnaround worth watching, not yet worth paying for.

Gap -0.68 at 34% above floor. Legacy packaged-food brands in volume decline, no breakup news since the Sept 19 refresh, consensus stuck at Hold and a ~$25 average target against a $24.73 price. Structural decline with no valuation compensation - sell.

Gap -0.03 with Ratio B 1.45x (60.3% downside against 41.6% upside) at 53.5% above floor. Waymo and Tesla are simultaneously partner and existential threat, and the price gives you no discount for that. Khosrowshahi's 141,000-share purchase at ~$70.96 on Sept 9 is the bull's best argument. Wait.

No longer classified as a turnaround. China share loss is simultaneous across VW, Audi and Porsche, the tariff burden is EUR4-5bn a year with no negotiating leverage, and CARIAD's record speaks for itself - that is a permanently lower earnings base. Gap -0.92 at 32.7% above the floor even after the profit warning and the Euro Stoxx 50 exit. ~4.4x earnings is not cheap enough. Avoid.

Gap -0.61 at 35.2% above floor with 51.8% downside. Consulting is the AI-deflation exposure and it is roughly half the company; the $1B CHIPS award and the 31-year dividend streak do not change that. Down ~22% YTD and still not cheap. Sell.

Gap exactly 0.00 with Ratio B 1.76x - no asymmetry at all. Agentic AI compressing per-seat pricing is the debate and Agentforce is the counter-bet; until one of them shows up in the numbers there is no reason to own the dispute at this price. Avoid.

Gap -0.29, Ratio B 1.74x, conservative 2-yr -14%. The pending Missouri ruling on the $7.25bn Roundup settlement is a genuine binary, but underneath it sits an unresolved Xarelto/Eylea patent cliff. Two problems, one price. Wait for the ruling.

Gap -1.35 with Ratio B 2.04x at 53.4% above floor. US cigarette volumes decline structurally, NJOY ACE remains banned from import and sale, and the 6.1% yield is being paid out of a shrinking base. Structural risk with no valuation support - sell.

Ratio B 8.35x and a conservative 2-yr case of -46% after a 5x run off the 2025 lows. The ~10% US government stake and 14A progress are real; the foundry economics are still unproven, and the price now assumes they work. This is the most expensive unproven turnaround in coverage. Sell into strength.

sections.heading: Sell / trim — priced for perfection or at a cycle peak
body: The twenty worst risk/reward setups in coverage: trim into strength, no new money.

items.x: Worst risk/reward in coverage: 532.9% above its $57.75 earnings-power floor with a -2.23 gap and spot above the bull case. Auto earnings have collapsed and the entire valuation rests on robotaxi and Optimus optionality with FY2026E adjusted EPS of $1.65. Sell.
Gap -1.51 at 573.2% above floor with Ratio B 3.57x, up 53.6% YTD to a fresh high. Permian volumes are real and entirely in the price; Mizuho at $320 and Scotiabank at $314 are chasing the tape. Trim.

Trading through its own bull case ($400) toward XBull with Ratio B mechanically at 118x and a -1.71 gap, 528% above floor. Crack spreads are at a geopolitical peak and Nymex 3:2:1 futures already show the 2027 roll-off. Sell.

89.2% downside against 8.0% upside (Ratio B 11.12x), conservative 2-yr -60%, gap -1.42, after crossing $1T market cap on a ~25% five-day run. The bull and xbull anchors had to be raised again just to keep up with the price. Sell.

Conservative 2-yr -73.2% - the worst in coverage - with Ratio B 17.92x because upside to the $280 bull case is down to 2.5% while downside to $150 is 45.1%. Four target raises in September chasing the same crack spreads. Sell.

Gap -2.12 with Ratio B 9.04x (66.7% downside against 7.4% upside) and a conservative 2-yr of -31%, at the 94th percentile of its range. Cook has confirmed a '100-year flood' in memory pricing and Apple is passing it through at ~28% higher ASPs - that protects margin and tests demand. Trim.

Gap -1.78 at 226% above floor with Ratio B 5.04x, near an all-time high after a 47% YTD run - while the row-crop replacement cycle is at a trough. Buying peak multiple on trough earnings is the exact mistake the framework exists to prevent. Sell.

Gap -1.43, Ratio B 6.41x, 246% above floor, 73x trailing earnings after a +6.6% jump on the Photonic Fabric announcement. Custom AI silicon is a hyperscaler capex cycle, and this is what the top of one looks like. Sell.

Gap -0.80 with Ratio B 3.38x (54.6% downside against 16.1% upside) and conservative 2-yr -35%, 200% above floor. Single-franchise Vyvgart concentration against live FcRn competition; the Forte Biosciences tuck-in does not diversify that. Trim.

Gap -1.67 with Ratio B 8.15x at 145% above floor. Asset-light franchising is a fine business; at 3.80 market-implied composite against a 2.12 adjusted composite you are paying for RevPAR that has not happened. Sell.
Spot is above the bull case, so Ratio B is infinite, with a -1.42 gap and 188% above floor after a ~140-152% year. Raymond James at $450 is the last argument standing. Sell into it.

Gap -1.32 with Ratio B 3.61x at 201% above floor, on record CEE refining ($14.5/bbl) and petrochemical (EUR381/t) margins. Peak-margin earnings capitalised at a peak multiple, with a state owner. Sell.

Ratio B 15.50x - the most extreme asymmetry in coverage - with a -1.79 gap at 102% above floor. The ad engine is healthy; the capex trajectory is the swing and the price assumes it resolves perfectly. Trim.

Ratio B 10.82x because upside to the $324 bull case has compressed to 5.5% while downside to bear is 59.6%; gap -1.48, conservative 2-yr -0.7%. FY2026 adjusted EPS guidance of $8.89-$9.01 is unchanged - the stock is not. Sell.

Ratio B 5.82x (83.1% downside against 14.3% upside) and a conservative 2-yr of -40%, 291% above a $45.45 floor. Revenue grew 93% YoY and the Rule of 40 reads 155 - genuinely exceptional, and entirely insufficient at this multiple. Trim.
Gap -1.15 with Ratio B 2.94x and a conservative 2-yr of -23%, at a fresh 52-week high 130% above floor. A Dutch retail bank priced for deposit margins that rate cuts will compress. Sell.
Gap -1.00, Ratio B 3.27x, 139% above floor, valued on two unreleased titles (Witcher 4 in 2028, Cyberpunk 2). Witcher 3 Remastered on Sept 29 is a cash event, not a thesis. Sell.

Ratio B 8.35x and a conservative 2-yr case of -46% after a 5x run off the 2025 lows. The ~10% US government stake and 14A progress are real; the foundry economics are still unproven, and the price now assumes they work. This is the most expensive unproven turnaround in coverage. Sell into strength.

Gap -1.31 with Ratio B 5.09x after a +7.5% move on the Sept 17 guidance raise (organic growth to 12%, data-center revenue +65% YoY) pushed the price to the $460 bull anchor. The AI capex cycle is in the numbers and in the multiple. Sell.
Gap -0.92 with Ratio B 3.61x at 88.9% above floor, Brent having pulled back from its ~$107-109 September high. An integrated major at a peak-cycle price. Trim.

The widest spread in the book: 8 compounders at a low price (AXP, BX, KKR, MA, MRSH, MUV2, SCHW, SPGI) against 14 names with no valuation support. The split is almost exactly fee businesses versus balance-sheet businesses - card networks, alternative managers, brokers and the ratings duopoly are cheap, while European and Polish banks (BBVA, BNP, INGA, ISP, NDA, PKO, UCG) sit at or near 52-week highs on peak NII with 2-yr conservative cases running from -18% to -25%. Every bank here shares one risk: the earnings being capitalised are cycle-peak earnings, and ING, Intesa and PKO in particular are priced for that peak to persist.

Ten names screen cheap and six of them are cheap for the same reason - the AI-fear basket (ACN, ADBE, INTU, NOW, SAP, WKL). Outside it, Oracle at a +1.94 gap and Adyen at +0.69 are the cheap franchises, while 14 names have no valuation support at all. The crowding is in AI supply: AMD at Ratio B 11.12x, Marvell at 6.41x, Meta at 15.50x, Apple at 9.04x. The shared risk cuts both ways - the same capex cycle that has re-rated the suppliers is what the software names are being discounted for surviving.

Nine cheap names, and they are the boring ones: auto parts (AZO, ORLY), home improvement (HD, LOW), restaurants (MCD, CMG), plus adidas and Hermes. The crowded end is autos and lodging - BMW, GM, MBG, VOW3, TSLA, HLT, MAR all sit with no valuation support, and Starbucks joins them today now that its turnaround has been re-rated as a completed one. Shared risk: the sector's cheap half is levered to a frozen housing and replacement cycle, the expensive half to tariffs and Chinese competition. Booking left this sector's compounder list for the AI basket.

The most one-sided sector in coverage: 12 names priced for perfection against three compounders at a low price (BSX, SNY, SYK). Stryker at 1.5% above floor and Sanofi at 16% are the only large-cap quality on offer at a price. The shared risk is patent arithmetic - Merck's Keytruda, Bristol's Eliquis and Opdivo, Pfizer's Eliquis and Ibrance, all 2028 - and the discriminator is whether the replacement pipeline is named and weighted or merely asserted. Pfizer was moved out of the structural bucket today on that test (Seagen ADCs carry its 53% bull case); Bristol was not, because its base case is simply pre-cliff earnings. Lilly is the one name where the growth is unarguable and the price already knows it.

Five cheap names (APD, SIE, TT, UPS, WM) against 15 with no support. The electrification and data-center trade is where the crowding is - Eaton at Ratio B 5.09x, GE Vernova at 1.83x and 291% above floor, Emerson at -1.31 - while the long-cycle machinery names (CAT at 3.29x, Deere at 5.04x) are at peak multiples on trough or peak earnings respectively. Shared risk: almost every industrial here is being valued on an order book, and order books are the last thing to break in a capex cycle.

One compounder at a low price (PEG, sitting 0.5% above its floor) out of 19 names, and six priced for perfection. The data-center load story has been fully capitalised - AEP at Ratio B 3.83x, Entergy at 4.46x, NextEra at 1.98x. The genuinely interesting utilities are the three special situations: EIX and PCG trade 24% and 20% below their earnings-power floors because California wildfire liability stayed uncapped when SB 492 died on Sept 1, and Dominion trades on the NextEra deal spread. Shared risk: long-end rates, and for the Californians, a legislature.

Three cheap (BN, MDLZ, PEP) against nine with no valuation support. Coca-Cola at Ratio B 2.53x and a -15% conservative 2-yr, Colgate at 99% above floor, L'Oreal at -0.93 - the defensive premium has been paid in full. Pepsi is the exception and it is cheap for an activist reason rather than an operating one. Shared risks: GLP-1 volume effects, which show up first in beverages and snacks, and a private-label shift that Kraft Heinz is already losing to.

Not one cheap name in 19. Thirteen carry too much cycle risk and three more are priced for perfection. Refining is the epicentre - Phillips 66 at a -73% conservative 2-yr, Marathon trading through its own bull case, Valero above it - on crack spreads that the forward curve itself rolls off in 2027. The integrateds (XOM, CVX, TTE) sit 89-281% above their floors on ~$100-105 Brent. Shared risk: every earnings estimate in this sector is a commodity price assumption, and the commodity is at a geopolitical premium.

The cheapest sector in the book on a class basis: three compounders at a low price (DTEGY, TMUS, VZ), nothing priced for perfection, and T-Mobile carrying a +1.49 gap at its 52-week low. Against that, the two cable names are cheap for the opposite reason - Comcast 33.5% below its floor and Charter with -172K broadband subscribers a quarter. The sector's shared risk is capital intensity meeting rate sensitivity: these are levered infrastructure businesses whose valuations move with the long end, which is exactly what took Deutsche Telekom down 7.6% in a week.

Nothing cheap. PPG is the only name with real downside protection (8.9% above floor, gap +0.05) and it is classed as a cyclical with the risk priced in rather than a bargain. Ecolab at -1.28 and 136% above floor is the clearest sell; BASF carries China overcapacity and EU energy costs with a -9% conservative 2-yr. Shared risk: Chinese export pressure on European producer margins, reiterated at APPEC 2026 and not going away.

Six names, none cheap, four fairly valued. Dow has the widest gap (+0.94) at trough earnings but sits 102% above its panic floor with a +3% conservative 2-yr - a cyclical option, not a compounder. KGHM and LyondellBasell carry too much cycle risk, the first on metals at record prices with a state owner, the second on polyolefins at a trough with leverage and a cut dividend. Shared risk: this sector's earnings are a spread, and both ends of it are set in China.

The 10-year sits at 5.00% after a hawkish repricing, with the FOMC median now showing one more 25bp hike this year and 4 of 12 members penciling two. The move was front-end led (2Y +16bp, 5Y +15bp, 30Y +1bp), flattening 2s10s to +25bp. The model reads the benchmark overvalued (gap -0.52). Prefer carry over duration - 2Y and 5Y - and watch the Sept and Oct CPI prints.

sections.heading: Main dangers across the book
body: Crowding at the top. 103 of 228 names - 45% of coverage - are priced for perfection or carry too much cycle risk. That is not a sector call, it is the whole book: quality compounders at 50 names and cyclicals at 46 are equally guilty. The dominant risk in this portfolio is not owning bad businesses, it is owning good ones at prices that already assume everything goes right.

Peak-cycle earnings capitalised at peak multiples. Refining (PSX, VLO, MPC, PKN), European banks (INGA, ISP, NDA, PKO, BNP, UCG), machinery (CAT, DE) and the electrification complex (ETN, GEV, EMR) all share one structure: the current earnings are the top of a cycle and the multiple on them is also at the top. The conservative 2-yr cases here run from -23% to -73%, which is the model saying the same thing twice.

The AI capex trade is now both sides of the book. Nvidia, AMD, Marvell, Broadcom, Micron, Eaton, GE Vernova, Vistra, Constellation and the pipelines are all levered to the same buildout, while Accenture, Adobe, Intuit, ServiceNow, SAP, Wolters Kluwer and now Booking are discounted for being on the losing end of it. A single change in the capex trajectory would move both groups - in opposite directions, but simultaneously, and the exposure is not diversified just because the signs differ.

Cheap because the earnings are contested. Comcast at 33.5% below its floor, Charter at a +0.90 gap with -172K broadband subscribers a quarter, Fiserv at -33.8% on an unproven Clover turnaround, Bristol on a 2028 cliff its own base case runs into, Intel on unproven foundry economics - nine names screen cheap while the E in the floor is exactly what is in dispute. The framework labels them rather than promoting them, and that label is the whole point: a floor built on an earnings estimate that is itself the question is not a floor.

Two uncapped legal tails. EIX and PCG trade 24% and 20% below their earnings-power floors because SB 492 died on Sept 1 without a wildfire liability cap - the downside is decided by the California legislature and the courts, not by the businesses. Add J&J's talc settlement at ~83% claimant support against a 95% threshold, 3M's PFAS long tail, and Bayer's pending Missouri Roundup ruling. These are position-sizing problems, not valuation problems.

Price-source ambiguity is recurring. This cycle flagged conflicting quotes on Kety (1152 / 1225 / 1265 PLN), Deutsche Bank (a stale EUR40.50 print), Air Liquide (EUR172.48 versus a converged EUR163-166), Estee Lauder, Halliburton, Parker Hannifin and Kone. Each was resolved to the value most consistent with the prior baseline and flagged rather than silently adopted, but classifications built on a wrong price are wrong in the same direction as the price.
